transport.finding: With a pressure- and creep-based wall the hot loop is a structural problem, not a pumping one. A 1800 K mean surface needs a ~1990 K coolant inlet at dT 300 K; Li then sits at ~2.0 MPa at the aft end of a 1.36 g burn (vapour pressure + subcooling + 0.85 MPa head), and at a 15 MPa creep allowable the walls weigh several times the coolant. H6a (two 60 % trunk pairs, six isolatable sections, heat-pipe fins, cross-feed) is the best fault-tolerant network at 2,282 t nominal (1,276-4,266 t correlated cases); H2 is lighter but a single puncture ends the burn. Material is the lever: the same network is 554 t with a 100 MPa, 3 t/m3 composite boundary.

ledgers.finding: Closing (excluding L1): coast (high-velocity, proactive), propulsion startup (preheat, 10 % power), drive trip (first 60 s), post-burn cooldown, black start (one unit, R1b), generator failure (two survivors at 100 %), coolant-sector failure in a burn (one H6a section), emergency (refuge, L3). Burns miss WARM by 0.37 MW even re-zoned (R5-D), because the hot-blade exchange debit (5.7 MW load with debit vs 5.3 MW usable); a defense engagement needs a thermal buffer of ~2.9 t of PCM per minute of engagement.

radiation_summary.finding: Verification passes: in a void model OpenMC reproduces the point kernel in every tank volume (ratio 0.95-1.09, mean 1.011), so the ship frame, the CSG placement and the normalisation agree with the generated model. With the shadow cone removed from the source, radiation scattered by the casing, blades and bulkhead still delivers 19 % (±10 % statistical) of the unshielded tank heating: ~54 W per unit at full power over the 13 tanks, 161 W for three units against a 118 W He-3 stage lift. Ring A sees 26 % of its unshielded neutron flux the same way. A shadow shield alone does not protect the tanks or the rings: side and structure shielding (or a longer standoff) is required. Scatter fractions only; no dose or safety claim.

problems.text: Hot-loop pressure boundary at ~2000 K and ~2 MPa: walls dominate the mass (V-B); no demonstrated material closes.
Coolant inlet ~1990 K is needed for an 1800 K mean surface (dT 300 K, 30 K drop): beyond Mo-TZM, at the Mo-Re/W-Re limit.
Dedicated L2 sections under strategy C break the 20 % HOT rule; only cross-strapped 750 K sections fit.
A forward-facing bulkhead emitter (R5-C) irradiates the He-3 tank zone; tank IR leak vs the 118 W lift decides it.
L1 conversion reject at ~900 K still has no radiator; the canon burn heat pumps dominate it (existing allocation).
Unit ramp rate after a trip is unknown; the conservative case drains the battery in a high band.
Frozen start: ~139 GJ of thaw and preheat before the first ignition; L2 alone takes days.
Hub ECLSS cross-ring duct through the rotating transfer drum not designed.
R5-B conflicts with the fixed aft edge (Q52 option D) and the engine exclusion rule.

3-D transport: structure scatter around the shadow cone reaches the He-3 tanks and ring A at a large fraction of the unshielded level; side/structure shielding needed; shield mass OPEN, no dose claim.

decisions.q: Adopt R5-A (750 K cross-strapped dual-header L2 sections, relocated bulkhead) as the radiator research baseline?
Adopt H6a (two 60 % trunk pairs, 6 isolatable sections, heat-pipe fins, cross-feed) as the hot-loop topology?
Accept a refractory-composite pressure boundary (~100 MPa, ~3 t/m3 at 2000 K) as a FICTIONAL-baseline assumption, with the research mass kept visible?
Keep Li as the coolant (Na, K near-critical; Sn too heavy under head; He-Xe pumping ~1 GW)?
Fictional L1: direct conversion of charged drive products with waste into the hot loop, closing the 900 K gap?
ECLSS: keep 7 units if the hub duct runs through the transfer drum; else 8 (4 + 4)?
LOG-G1: 3 t gross containers (single-arm handling) instead of 6 t?
Next: 3-D transport with weight windows to quote shield transmission (beyond the scatter split)?
